  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR

  4:00 P.M.
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted
upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City
Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.

ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS TO THE AGENDA: Additions to the agenda are limited by California Government
Code Section 54954.2 of the Brown Act and for those items that arise after the posting of the Agenda and must
be acted upon prior to the next City Council meeting.

ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL COMMENTS: Announcements, Committee Reports
and Council Comments are for the purpose of presenting brief comments or reports, are subject to California
Government Code Section 54954.2 of the Brown Act and are limited to 15-minutes per meeting.

CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS: All matters listed under Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and all
will be enacted by one roll call vote. There will be no discussion of these items unless members of the City
Council request specific items to be removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion. Any member of
the public may address the Council on items on the Consent Calendar. Public comments on any item or items on
the consent calendar are limited to three minutes per speaker. If you wish to speak to a particular item or items,
please complete a Speaker’s Form and give it to the City Clerk. (Please see information in “Request to Speak”
section.

PUBLIC COMMENT: Any member of the public may address the City Council on items within the Council’s
subject matter jurisdiction but which are not listed on this agenda during public comments. However, no action
may be taken on matters that are not part of the posted agenda. Public comments are scheduled for 30 minutes
and are limited to three minutes per person. If you wish to speak, please complete a Speaker’s Form and submit
to the City Clerk.
 CITY COUNCIL – NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

SPEAKER’S CARD/REQUEST TO SPEAK: If you would like to address the City Council on a scheduled agenda
item, please complete the speaker’s card. The card is at the table at the entrance to the Council Chamber. Please
identify on the card your name, address, and the item on which you would like to speak and return to the City
Clerk. The speaker’s card assists the Mayor in ensuring that all persons wishing to address the Council are
recognized. Your name will be called at the time the matter is heard by the Council.

STAFF REPORTS: As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or
organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with
the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying. If you have any questions regarding any item of
business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda
item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949) 724-6205.

PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public Hearings are scheduled for a time certain of 4:00 p.m. (unless noticed otherwise) or
as soon thereafter as possible. City Council, when considering the matter scheduled for hearing, will take the
following actions: 1) Open the Public Hearing. 2) Receive staff report. 3) Accept public testimony. 4) City Council
comments and questions. 5) Take appropriate action. Those wishing to address the City Council during the Public
Hearing must complete a “Request to Speak” form and provide it to the City Clerk prior to the hearing. If, in the
future, you wish to challenge in court any of the matters on this agenda for which a public hearing is to be
conducted, you may be limited to raising only those issues which you (or someone else) raised orally at the public
hearing or in written correspondence received by the City at or before the hearing. Any person seeking to
challenge a City Council decision made as a result of a proceeding in which by law a hearing is required to be
given, evidence is required to be taken, and the discretion in the determination of facts is vested in the City
Council, shall be required to commence that action 90 days following the date on which the decision becomes
final as provided in Code of Civil Procedure Section 1094.6. Please refer to Code of Civil Procedure 1094.6 to
determine how to calculate when a decision becomes “final.” Notice: Public Hearings listed for continuance will
be continued as noted and posting of this agenda serves as notice of continuation. Any matter not noted for
continuance, will be posted separately.

AMERICANS WITH DISABILITIES ACT: It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With
Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special
assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every
reasonable manner. Please contact Jeri L. Stately, City Clerk, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to inform us
of your particular needs and to determine if accommodation is feasible. Please advise us at the time if you will
need accommodations to attend or participate in meetings on a regular basis.

This agenda was prepared by the City Clerk. Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and
fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. However, study sessions and/or closed sessions are periodically
held prior to the start of the regular meeting. The City Council Agenda is posted in the Police Department and
available at your local library. It is also available through our FAX LIBRARY system. Simply dial (949) 724-6210
and request document number 100 anytime after 5:00 p.m. on the Friday prior to a City Council meeting. The
Agenda may also be accessed through the City’s web page at www.ci.irvine.ca.us

MINUTES

  IRVINE
  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  March 22, 2005

CALL TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order on March 22, 2005 at
4:01 p.m., in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza,
Irvine, California, by Mayor Krom, presiding officer.

ROLL CALL

  PRESENT:  5  COUNCILMEMBER:  Larry Agran
  COUNCILMEMBER:  Steven Choi
  COUNCILMEMBER:  Christina Shea
  MAYOR PRO TEM:  Sukhee Kang
  MAYOR:  Beth Krom

  ABSENT:  0  COUNCILMEMBER  None

Also present were Assistant City Manager, Sean Joyce; Assistant City Manager, Wally
Kreutzen; Deputy City Attorney, Jeff Melching; Director of Public Safety, David L.
Maggard, Director of Administrative Services, Rick Paikoff; Director of Public Works,
Marty Bryant; Acting Director of Community Services, John McAllister; Director of
Community Development, Tina Christiansen; City Clerk, Jeri L. Stately; Deputy City
Clerk, Teri Beach; and Sergeant At Arms, David Tran.
 City Council Minutes  March 22, 2005

STUDY SESSION - STRATEGIC PLAN FOR CHILDREN AND FAMILIES

Mayor Krom introduced Professor Sid Garner and Dr. Lisa Henson who gave a brief
report. (Exhibit Nos. 1 and 2 on file in the City Clerk’s Department.)

City Council discussion included funding a bi-annual indicator’s report to measure the
City’s progress; need to provide assistance to families to identify earned income tax
credits; consideration of increasing staffing level by one full time equivalent person to
work year round to ensure benefits from program emerge; need to identify pilot
partnership programs with Irvine Unified School District; utilize outside sources to assist
with funding of programs; expansion of DARE Program to include junior high and high
school age kids; and identify mechanism for funding of strategic partners.

No action was taken on this item.

RECESS

Mayor Krom introduced Deputy City Attorney, Jeff Melching, who cited the Closed
Sessions.

Mayor Krom recessed the meeting at 4:47 p.m. to Closed Session.

CLOSED SESSION

10.  LIABILITY CLAIMS (Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.95)

  Two Cases: Kim vs. City of Irvine;
  Tony Fausto vs. City of Irvine

11.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE APPOINTMENT (Pursuant to Government Code
  Section 54957)

  Position Title: Acting City Manager

RECONVENE TO THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING

Mayor Krom reconvened the meeting to regular session at 5:11 p.m.

Deputy City Attorney, Jeff Melching announced that pursuant to Government Code
54957.1(a)5 and by unanimous vote, the City Council appointed an Acting City
Manager.

  2
 City Council Minutes  March 22, 2005

Mayor Krom announced that the appointment of Acting City Manager was made to
Sean Joyce and will be effective June 1, 2005.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Councilmember Choi led the Pledge of Allegiance.

MOMENT OF SILENCE

Mayor Krom requested a moment of silence and suggested that in honor of World
Water Day reflection be given to the victims of the tsunami in South Asia.

MUSICAL PRESENTATION

Mayor Krom introduced The Irvine Chinese Chorus who performed, "The Star Spangled
Banner" followed by "Impatiens."

PRESENTATIONS

1)  Mayor Krom recognized the contributors and volunteers of the "Irvine Cares:
  Music of Love" Fund Raising Event held on February 27, 2005 which benefited
  victims of the Tsunami in South Asia. (Exhibit No. 3 on file in the City Clerk’s
  Department.)

2)  Mayor Krom presented Family Friendly Business Awards to the following:
  • Joe DiCorpo, Vice President, Administration - Motorcycle Industry Council.
  • John Hogan, President – Hall & Forman, Inc.
  • Kristina Hiiitgen, Vice President of Associate Services – Option One
  Mortgage Corporation.

3)  Mayor Krom introduced Marshall Kaplan, Executive Director of the Merage
  Foundation who gave a presentation on “Children First.” .” (Exhibit No. 4 on file
  in the City Clerk’s Department)

4)  Mayor Krom introduced Director of Public Safety/Chief of Police, Dave Maggard;
  Sergeant Henry Boggs; Sergeant Barry Aninag (Coordinator of Irvine’s Explorer
  Post); Police Officer, Mario Casas; and members of the Irvine Police Department
  Explorer Post. Sergeant Boggs, representing the Fraternal Order of Police,
  California State Lodge, presented a grant check Chief of Police, Dave Maggard
  and Sergeant Barry Aninag who accepted a check in the amount of $2,000 on
  behalf of the Irvine Police Explorer Post.

  3
 City Council Minutes  March 22, 2005

INTRODUCTIONS

Mayor Krom announced that Assistant City Manager Sean Joyce would be assisting the
Council at the dais in the absence of City Manager, Allison Hart.

Mayor Krom announced that Deputy City Attorney, Jeff Melching would be assisting the
Council at the dais in the absence of City Attorney, Joel Kuperberg.

ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

Councilmember Shea recognized the following individuals in the community:
• Dr. R. Duncan Luce, research professor at UCI and Emeritus of Cognitive Science
  was honored at the White House by George W. Bush and received the National
  Medal of Science; and
• UCI Senior Brittany Sheik; is the University’s first recipient of the George Mitchell
  Scholarship and will be presented a State Assembly Resolution by Chuck Devore on
  Wednesday; and
• On March 26, the University High School Theatre Guild and Ensemble Choir will
  host a flea market and carwash in the school’s parking lot.

Mayor Pro Tempore Kang recognized Jim Lizzi, Public Works Department, for his
assistance to Irvine residents Kevin Chard and Robert Ferman in helping to replace
trees along Harvard Avenue.

Councilmember Choi made the following comments:
• Appreciation to City staff for scheduling a meeting to welcome the delegation from
  Kwangju, South Korea for the purpose of establishing a sister city relationship with
  South Korea; and
• Appreciation to Chief Dave Maggard for his update on the City’s crime statistics; and
• Noted he met with Irvine Division Fire Chief Matt Vadala for an overview on the Fire
  Authority’s role.

Mayor Krom made the following announcements:
• In celebration of the Week of the Child, the Irvine Child Care Committee and the

 City Council Minutes  March 22, 2005

  City Council discussion included clarification that City has a practice with
  respect to financial statements; clarification the City requires assurances that
  money is being spent correctly; clarification that audited financial statements
  are not always required; clarification when dealing with restricted funds or
  other circumstances that apply, that an audited financial statement may be
  required.

  ACTION: It was moved by Councilmember Shea, seconded by Mayor Pro
  Tempore Kang, to:

  1) Authorize the City to extend to the Orange County Great Park Corporation
  a cash advance of $2,122,250 subject to reimbursement upon execution
  of the Great Park Development Agreement.

  2) Rescind the following action taken at the November 9, 2004, City Council
  meeting:

  a)  “The City Council agreed that the City would not exceed the
  $250,000 amount of monies allotted to the Great Park Board to be used
  for doing business with the Great Park Conservancy without an audited
  financial statement, and that the City would not do any business with the
  Great Park Conservancy without receiving an audited financial statement.”

  By rescission of the above action, the following action replaces the action
  taken on November 9, 2004:

  b)  The City Council agreed that any future allocations of money to any
  non-profit organization that conducts business with the City will be
  required to follow the standard City financial practices and/or procedures
  required of any non-profit organization that requests moneys from the City.
